card.name: Verbs and links in manner phrases
card.fires_on: Verbs or small linking words that come just before a manner or extent phrase, such as 'to great lengths', 'with abandon', 'like a lady' or 'at all costs'. It shows up in general web prose about behavior, character and quotations.

modes.label: Verb before extent phrase
modes.description: A verb such as go, walk or agree that leads into a phrase of extreme or manner-style action.
modes.example: It can also mean that you hate conflict and would<< go>> to great lengths to not be involved in

modes.label: Link before manner
modes.description: A small word like with, like or as that introduces how something is done.
modes.example: Cooking is like love. It should be entered into<< with>> abandon or not at all.

card.plain: It fires on words that set up how someone does something, such as with abandon or like a lady.
